subject: Audit rights: trigger framework, evidence timetable & pen-test escalation
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Young <claire.young@medinova.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medinova.com>, legal@medinova.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Audit rights: trigger framework, evidence timetable & pen-test escalation

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Per our call I wanted to put a short, pragmatic proposal on the table so your legal and security teams can review without digging through the full MSA redline. The goal: give you deterministic triggers for inspection/pen-test access, a lightweight evidence handoff cadence, and a narrow escalation path for higher-sensitivity requests.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Trigger framework: 3 discrete triggers that allow inspection access — (1) regulatory audit request, (2) confirmed security incident attributed to Redwood infrastructure, (3) contractual compliance review once per 12 months. Each trigger maps to a scoped evidence bundle and access window.
- Evidence timetable: weekly sprint-style handoffs for typical SOC2 artifact requests (owner matrix attached). For more invasive asks (forensic logs, raw DB exports) we propose a 10-business-day formal evidence window with security review.
- Pen-test notice: standard 15-business-day notice for external pentests; we will provide a Doc that standardises target scope and blast-radius limits (attached). For emergency/incident-driven pentests we propose an expedited 3-business-day window with our on-call engineers looped.

Action items for Medinova Legal/Security:
1) Confirm you are comfortable with the three trigger categories above (regulatory, incident, annual).
2) Flag any clauses in your standard order form that require broader inspection rights than this framework.
3) If accepted, we will prepare a one-paragraph Security Exhibit addition and a short schedule to be appended to the order form.

Attachments: evidence-ownership-matrix.xlsx (owners + example artifacts), pen-test-notice-template.docx (scope/notice template).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if useful.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---

On Sun, 22 Aug 2027 at 11:12 AM Claire Young <claire.young@medinova.com> wrote:
> Thanks Hannah — this is helpful and much clearer than the MSA text we pulled. Two quick clarifications from our side:
>
> 1) For "regulatory audit request" — does that include our external auditors (KPMG) when they request a scoped snapshot? We need to be able to give them the artifacts under our SOC2 processes.
> 2) For pen-tests: 15 business days is reasonable for standard tests, but can you define "blast-radius limits" in the template? Our security team requires a non-destructive clause.
>
> I'll run this by our legal and security folks and get back by Wednesday.
>
> -Claire
> Senior Security Program Manager
> Medinova


On Mon, 23 Aug 2027 at 10:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hannah / team —
>
> I pulled a first-pass redline for a compact Security Exhibit that maps to Hannah's framework. Key legal points I've attempted to narrow:
>
> - Clarify that "regulatory audit" includes auditor access where the customer is the subject (i.e., KPMG for Medinova). We will provide the same artifact set we provide to SOC2 assessors, subject to NDAs.
> - Limit inspection windows to explicit date ranges and a maximum of two evidence handoff sprints per 12-month period unless mutually agreed to escalate.
> - Include a non-destructive pen-test clause: external tests may not compromise evidence integrity or production availability; Redwood has the right to require a staging-only test if risk exceeds threshold.
> - Define an expedited escalation path: incident-driven requests can compress timelines (e.g., 3-business-day notice) but require a pre-agreed on-call contact and a three-party triage call within 24 hours of request.
>
> I'm attaching suggested MSA wording separately (I'll paste the clause below). If legal@medinova wants, we can include a one-paragraph bridge in the order form that points to the Security Exhibit rather than baking long language into the MSA.
>
> Proposed insertion (short form):
> "Security Exhibit — Audit & Inspection: Customer may request inspection access under the following triggers: (a) regulatory audit of Customer, (b) incident materially impacting Customer data controls, (c) annual compliance review. For each trigger Redwood will provide a scoped evidence bundle and temporary access where necessary. Inspection windows will be scoped and limited; non-destructive pen-testing is permitted following a minimum notice period, and Redwood reserves rights to require staging tests for high-risk surface areas. Expedited incident-driven reviews follow the triage and on-call process specified in Appendix A."
>
> Please review and let me know if anything needs to be stronger/softer. Hannah, Monica: anything from an ops/owner perspective?
>
> -Karthik
> Sr. Counsel, Contracts
> Redwood Inference


On Mon, 23 Aug 2027 at 13:40 PM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Adding the evidence ownership and cadence perspective here. I updated the attached Excel with concrete owners and a sample 4-week sprint:
>
> Week 0: Intake & scoping (customer submits request; our Security triages to owner list)
> Week 1: Artifact collection (SOC2 controls mapping, configuration screenshots, exported logs summary)
> Week 2: Redaction & validation (we apply agreed PII minimisation; security validates exports)
> Week 3: Delivery & wrap-up (handoff link + short postmortem if requested)
>
> For forensic-grade asks (raw logs, full packet captures) we mark those as "elevated" and use the 10-business-day evidence window with 2-person engineer review.
>
> Notes/asks for Medinova:
> - Please run the owners matrix against your contact list and flag any overlaps.
> - If KPMG will be used as your auditor, we require a short engagement letter naming Redwood as a permitted provider under your audit scope.
>
> I'll keep the workbook in the drive link Hannah shared and will export a printer-friendly PDF for your legal team if requested.
>
> Thanks,
> Monica Patel
> Senior Manager, Assurance Operations
> Redwood Inference
>

On Tue, 24 Aug 2027 at 16:22:00 -0700 Alex Torres <alex.torres@medinova.com> wrote:
> Hi all — polite + quick from Medinova legal/security: we reviewed the proposed framework and the 3-trigger model looks reasonable. A couple of concrete asks:
>
> 1) Can Redwood confirm that the "maximum of two evidence handoff sprints per 12-month period" is per "account" and not per order form? Our procurement team manages multiple subscriptions and we need this to be account-level.
> 2) We need the non-destructive pen-test clause spelled out with language that allows for cryptographic key material to be out-of-scope. Can Karthik draft the specific sentence and circulate?
>
> We also appreciate the sprint cadence — Claire's team will compare owners this week and circle back with any name changes. If we can get a short Security Exhibit PDF and the pen-test clause in redline form by Friday, we can push the order form through procurement the following week.
>
> Best,
> Alex Torres
> Director, Security Engineering
> Medinova
